When you update an existing gateway, leaving out authentication keeps its current setting. If you try to turn off authentication after it is on, the API returns HTTP 400.

Existing gateways with authentication turned off can continue without it. You can turn it on in your gateway settings or include authentication: true in a gateway update request:

Before turning authentication on, configure HTTP clients to send a valid Cloudflare API token. Requests through Workers bindings remain pre-authenticated.

For setup instructions and supported authorization headers, refer to AI Gateway authentication.

item.title: Browser Run - Crawl results include URL outcomes and robots.txt diagnostics
item.description:
Browser Run /crawl results now include more detailed diagnostics. Each URL record can include an outcome that identifies the specific processing result, such as success, robots_disallowed, timeout, or page_error.

The job-level robots array reports the robots.txt state for up to 50 origins encountered by the crawl. Each entry includes the origin, whether usable rules were available, and the HTTP status when the crawler received a response.

For field definitions and all possible outcome values, refer to URL outcomes and robots.txt diagnostics.

item.title: R2 - Request metrics breakdown by region and HTTP error code
item.description:
You can now compare regional activity and errors by HTTP status code on the Metrics page for a R2 bucket in the Cloudflare dashboard.

Go to Bucket metrics ↗

Compare regions

Use Request Distribution by Region to compare request activity and filter by writes, reads, errors, or rate-limited errors (429).

Inspect errors

Use Errors by Status Code to compare error counts and trends.

To troubleshoot errors, refer to the R2 error code reference.

item.title: AI Search - AI Search billing postponed to December 1, 2026, and default sync interval is now 24 hours
item.description:
Billing postponed to December 1, 2026

AI Search billing has been postponed by one month and now begins on December 1, 2026, instead of November 1, 2026. You will not be charged for AI Search usage before December 1, 2026. Pricing and included usage are unchanged.

For rates and included usage, refer to Limits & pricing.

Default sync interval is now 24 hours

The default sync interval for AI Search instances is changing from 6 hours to 24 hours. You can still choose any supported interval, from 15 minutes to 24 hours, with the Sync interval setting in your instance settings or the sync_interval field in the API.

For details, refer to Sync interval.

item.title: Flagship - Evaluate Flagship flags locally
item.description:
Flagship bindings now evaluate flags against a local flag store during local development, instead of calling your remote app. You can develop offline and test flag changes without affecting production. This applies to wrangler dev, the Cloudflare Vite plugin, the Vitest integration, and cf dev.

The local store starts empty, so evaluations return the default value you pass in code. Add and manage local flags in any of these ways:

  • Wrangler — Add --local to wrangler flagship flags commands, such as create, update, and evaluate. To copy all flags from your remote app, run npx wrangler flagship flags pull <APP_ID>.
  • Local Explorer — Create, edit, toggle, and evaluate flags in Local Explorer while your dev server runs.
  • cf CLI — Add --local to cf flagship commands.

To keep evaluating against your remote app instead, set remote: true on the binding.

The local flag store requires Wrangler v4.135.0 or @cloudflare/vite-plugin v1.56.0 or later. Flagship in Local Explorer requires Wrangler v4.148.0 or @cloudflare/vite-plugin v1.63.0 or later.

Refer to Flagship local development for details.

item.title: Workers - Workers will use the new module registry by default on November 17
item.description:
Starting November 17, 2026, JavaScript Workers with a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later will use the new module registry by default. You will no longer need the new_module_registry flag for these dates. Python Workers keep using the legacy registry.

The module registry finds and loads JavaScript modules in your Worker. We announced the new registry in September 2026 ↗︎. It improves compatibility with JavaScript standards and Node.js. In Workers using Node.js compatibility, you can use require() to load ES modules. The module and its dependencies must not use top-level await.

You can also use import.meta to get information about the current module and find the URL of another module without loading it:

When deployed with src/index.ts as the unbundled entrypoint, isEntrypoint is true. helperUrl is a URL within your Worker bundle. Resolving the URL does not check whether the module exists or load it over the network. Build tools may transform import.meta. To try this example directly, refer to unbundled deployments.

Existing Workers keep their current behavior until you change their compatibility date or flags. To try the new registry before November 17, keep your current date and add new_module_registry to your compatibility flags.

Before updating, check your dependencies for invalid import attributes and changes to require() behavior. The new registry rejects invalid import attributes. Calls to require() also fail if the module or any of its dependencies use top-level await. To keep the legacy registry with a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later, add legacy_module_registry.

For migration details, refer to the new module registry compatibility flag, bundling documentation, and Node.js compatibility documentation.

item.title: Workers - Request.signal will be enabled by default in Workers on November 17
item.description:
Starting November 17, 2026, Workers with a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later will receive client disconnection events through request.signal by default. Use these events to stop unnecessary work when a client leaves. You will no longer need the enable_request_signal compatibility flag for these dates.

We introduced this feature in May 2025. You can log cancellations, clean up resources, or cancel operations that accept an AbortSignal.

For example, this Worker logs a client disconnection and cancels an outgoing request:

Existing Workers keep their current behavior until you change their compatibility date or flags. To try this feature before November 17, keep your current date and add enable_request_signal to your compatibility flags.

With a compatibility date of 2026-11-17 or later, add disable_request_signal to opt out. This change does not enable request_signal_passthrough. Pass the signal explicitly, as the example does.

For more information, refer to the Request API and the Request.signal compatibility flag.

item.title: Browser Run - Browser Run now runs Chrome 152
item.description:
Browser Run now runs Chrome 152 by default. Your sessions get current web platform features, rendering fixes, and security patches. You do not need to change your code.

This release also includes the following improvements:

  • Updated default User-Agent. The default User-Agent for Quick Actions now reports Chrome 152 instead of Chrome 119. If you allowlist or match the Browser Run User-Agent, update your rules. You can still set your own value with the userAgent parameter. Refer to Automatic request headers.
  • Better site compatibility. Quick Actions requests now look more like requests from a regular Chrome browser, so fewer sites block them.
  • Large response headers. Pages that return large response headers now load correctly.
  • Updated root certificates. Browser Run removed distrusted root certificates from its trust store.
  • Absolute links. /links now returns absolute URLs, and links-only crawls now follow relative links.
  • Better Markdown output. /markdown and crawl Markdown output now keep code block languages.
  • Clearer errors. Quick Actions that time out now return a consistent error. Outbound Workers that throw an exception now return an HTTP error to the browser.

For more information, refer to the Browser Run documentation.

item.title: D1 - D1 will enforce a maximum query result size of 50 MB
item.description:
Beginning Wednesday, November 4, 2026, D1 will enforce a maximum query result size of 50 MB. Queries that return a result larger than 50 MB will fail and return the following error:

The 50 MB limit covers the 99.999th percentile of requests across D1, so most D1 users will not be impacted.

Import and export operations via the REST API are not subject to this limit and will continue to work as they do today.

If your queries return large results, reduce the result size before the enforcement date. For example, select only the columns you need instead of using SELECT *, and paginate large result sets with LIMIT and OFFSET.

For more information, refer to D1 limits and the D1 error list.

item.title: Durable Objects, Workers - Durable Objects now defer code updates by default
item.description:
Durable Objects can stay active across requests, allowing you to run long-running agents, maintain long-lived WebSocket connections and coordinate state across many clients. This is possible because each Durable Object is globally unique, and this means it must run only one version of your code at a time. Previously, when you deployed a change to your Durable Objects code, that change would be applied immediately, which could interrupt in-flight work and terminate open connections.

Durable Objects now defer code updates by default. When you deploy, an active Durable Object can keep running its current code for up to 5 minutes (300 seconds) while it waits to hibernate. This gives in-flight work time to finish. WebSocket connections that use the Hibernation API remain connected when an object adopts new code after hibernating.

For an active Durable Object, a code update follows this flow:

flowchart TD
    accTitle: Code updates for an active Durable Object
    accDescr: By default, an active object can keep running its current code until it hibernates or the delay ends. After hibernating, it starts on new code on the next request. If the delay ends first, or immediate mode is selected, it resets and adopts the new code. Deferral is best effort.
    A["You deploy new code"] -->|"Default: deferred"| B["The object can keep running<br/>its current code"]
    B --> C{"Hibernates before<br/>the delay ends?"}
    C -->|Yes| D["Starts on the new code<br/>on the next request"]
    C -->|No| E["The object resets<br/>and adopts the new code"]
    A -.->|"Override: immediate"| E

To change the delay, add code_update_strategy to durable_objects in your Wrangler configuration:

max_delay is in seconds, from 0 to 86400 (24 hours), with millisecond precision. Omit it to use the default of 300 seconds.

To set the strategy for a single deployment, pass --durable-objects-code-update-mode with immediate or deferred <duration>. For example, apply an update right away during an incident, or when your deployment tooling calls a Durable Object right after deploying and needs the new code:

npx wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate
yarn wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate
pnpm wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate

A deferred code update is best effort and does not guarantee that every operation finishes. The object can still reset before max_delay is reached, for example during a Cloudflare runtime update.

For more information, including how this interacts with gradual deployments and the REST API, refer to Durable Objects code updates.

item.title: Workers, BYOIP, Bots - Workers subrequests now preserve context for BYOIP destinations
item.description:
Cloudflare now preserves Workers context when a subrequest targets a Cloudflare-proxied hostname using Bring Your Own IP (BYOIP). These requests are identified as Cloudflare-to-Cloudflare traffic instead of external Internet traffic.

Previously, some BYOIP subrequests could lose Workers context and original client signals. This could cause security rules to behave unexpectedly, Bot Management to evaluate an internal Cloudflare connection instead of the original client, or affected requests to return false 403 responses.

Workers subrequests to BYOIP destinations now preserve the CF-Worker header and cf.worker.upstream_zone field. This supports consistent security rule evaluation across same-zone and cross-zone subrequests.

Bot Management fields on the destination zone now represent the original end-user connection for affected BYOIP subrequests. Bot scores, verified bot status, and JA3/JA4 fingerprints no longer represent the internal connection between Cloudflare services.

Because Cloudflare-proxied BYOIP destinations now follow standard Workers subrequest handling, cross-zone requests set CF-Connecting-IP to the Workers client IP address 2a06:98c0:3600::103 for security reasons. This applies when a Worker in one Cloudflare zone sends a subrequest to a hostname in another Cloudflare zone. Same-zone subrequests continue to reflect the client IP through CF-Connecting-IP.

For more information, refer to Cloudflare BYOIP, Workers subrequests, and CF-Connecting-IP in Worker subrequests.

item.title: Agents - Agents SDK: Agent Skills are files in your agent's Workspace
item.description:
Agent Skills in the Cloudflare Agents SDK are now files. Write a folder with a SKILL.md into your agent's Computer ↗︎ Workspace, under /workspace/.agents/skills/, and the agent can use it on its next turn. You do not need a build step or a deploy, and the agent can write its own skills.

This release includes:

  • Three sources. Load skills from a Computer Workspace, an R2 bucket, or code. Think lists every source again before each turn.
  • The open format. Every SKILL.md is checked against the Agent Skills specification ↗︎. As the specification's guide for agents recommends, a skill that breaks a rule still loads, with a logged warning. Use parseSkill() to check a skill before you write it.
  • Scripts in the Workspace. Skill scripts are Workspace files, and the model runs them with the Workspace exec tool. Refer to Execution.
  • Skill tools for any harness. Use the same activate_skill and read_skill_resource tools in Think, Pi Durable, or the AI SDK. Refer to Skills tools.
  • Warm prompt caches. When a skill changes mid-conversation, Think sends the new catalog as a reminder instead of rebuilding the cached system prompt. An overridden getSystemPrompt() now stays at the top of the system prompt, above context blocks.

This is a breaking change for code that uses agents/skills directly. The agents:skills Vite import, agents/skills/compile, SkillRegistry, and Think's skillWorkspace are removed, and runner() moved to agents/skills/runner. Install Agents SDK v0.32.0 ↗︎ and Think v0.23.0 ↗︎ or later. Refer to the computer-skills ↗︎ and r2-skills ↗︎ examples.

item.title: Agents, Browser Run - Agents SDK: Preview dev servers in the browser without public URLs
item.description:
Agents that build websites need to check their work in a real browser. Internal hostnames let your agent's browser preview a dev server running in a container without exposing that server to the public Internet.

With internal hostnames, the persistent browser in the Cloudflare Agents SDK can open sites that only your agent serves. Give the browser hostnames such as preview.internal, and its requests to them go to your agent instead of the Internet. The model can check a dev server in its sandbox, a folder in its workspace, or another Worker in the same browser it uses for the web, and nothing is exposed publicly.

Each internal host has a fetch function that runs in your Durable Object, so it can use the object's bindings and state. A host can also send its requests straight to another Worker through a service binding. Add a target schema to a host, and the model chooses what it serves, such as which port or which folder.

Internal hostnames are a capability of the browser, independent of your agent harness. Use the built-in adapters for Pi Durable, AI SDK, and TanStack AI, or connect another harness by implementing a tool with browser.session(). No prebuilt adapter is required.

This example adds a private dev-server preview to a Pi Durable agent. Start with that guide's packages, bindings, and request handler, and install Agents SDK v0.31.0 ↗︎ or later. The example has three parts:

  • Browser configuration: internalHosts defines how the browser reaches the dev server.
  • Durable Object wiring: Lifecycle and fetchInternalHost() connect the browser to your application.
  • Harness integration: browserTool from agents/browser/pi registers the tool with Pi.

To use another harness, keep the browser configuration. Choose a browser-tool adapter if one is available, or implement a tool using browser.session().

browserTool tells the model about each host, including the schema of its target. Because preview.internal has a target schema, the model can choose which port it serves. To check its dev server, the model calls browser.assignHost() with a target that matches the schema, such as { port: 5173 }, and opens the URL it gets back:

The target is checked against the schema and stored, so it lasts across turns, browser restarts, and redeploys. Each request to http://preview.internal/ then calls the host's fetch function with { port: 5173 }.

This release also simplifies browserTool. It runs the model's code in its own Dynamic Worker and no longer needs a CodemodeRuntime export. Refer to the v0.31.0 upgrade notes ↗︎ if you already use browserTool.

For the complete example, limits, and security guidance, refer to Internal hostnames.

item.title: Workers VPC - Select a virtual network for VPC Network bindings
item.description:
VPC Network bindings can select a specific virtual network by setting network_id to cf1:vnet:<UUID>, where the UUID is the ID of the virtual network. Continue to use cf1:network to select your account's default virtual network.

Multiple bindings can select different virtual networks. This lets one Worker reach separate backends that use the same private IP address:

For details, refer to VPC Networks configuration.

item.title: Workers - Workers Builds now retains builds and build logs for 90 days
item.description:
Workers Builds now retains each build and its build logs for 90 days after the build finishes. You can find them under View build history in your Worker's Deployments tab, or through the Workers Builds API.

After 90 days, a build and its logs are removed. The versions and deployments it created stay in your Worker's version history, so you can still roll back to them.

If you need a build's logs for longer, you can download them with the Get build logs API endpoint.

For more information, refer to the Workers Builds limits documentation.

item.title: Workflows, Workers - Restrict Workflows to a jurisdiction
item.description:
You can now restrict a Workflow to a jurisdiction. Its instances only run and store data within that jurisdiction, which helps you comply with data localization regulations such as GDPR ↗︎ or FedRAMP ↗︎.

Set jurisdiction on a workflows binding, or on a Workflow declared in exports:

The supported jurisdictions are eu (the European Union), us (the United States), and fedramp (FedRAMP-Moderate data centers).

A Workflow's jurisdiction is set when the Workflow is created, and cannot be changed afterwards. If an existing Workflow has a different jurisdiction, wrangler deploy and wrangler versions upload stop before uploading your Worker.

Workflow jurisdictions require Wrangler 4.152.0 or above.

For more information, refer to Data location.

item.title: Agents, Workers - Cloudflare Computer now helps agents recover from interruptions and wait for approval
item.description:
@cloudflare/computer ↗︎ gives your agent a workspace to run code in. From v0.7.0, that code can resume after a deploy or crash, and pause on an external action, for example to approve a tool call.

Resume interrupted runs

Set onInterrupt: "replay" on WorkerJavaScriptBackend, or on a single run.

When recovery is triggered, the JavaScript runs again from the beginning, reusing recorded results for completed calls without printing previously recorded output again. If a call's result was not recorded before the interruption, recovery may repeat the call — even if its action already succeeded. For retry handling, including unsafeToRepeat() for operations that cannot safely repeat, refer to Calls that must not run twice.

Recovery starts on the next call to workspace.runtime. To recover without waiting for traffic, call workspace.runtime.recover() from a Durable Object alarm.

Wait for approvals

Expose your application functions through custom modules. A function can call ctx.interrupt() to pause the run until your application supplies an approval decision.

Require approval before posting a comment

For example, to provide a GitHub module that allows an agent to post a comment on an issue with approval, an implementation of postComment could look like this:

Call it from agent code

When the agent's code calls postComment(), the run pauses at ctx.interrupt() until your app responds. The agent's code calls it like any other function:

Respond to the approval request

The time spent waiting does not count toward its timeout. The wait also survives deploys. Fetch the pending calls with workspace.runtime.pending() and resolve them with respond():

The run continues once all pending calls are resolved.

For setup, current limitations, and how replay works, refer to Resume runs after a restart.

item.title: Workers - Workers tracing — new spanContext(), setStatus(), and updateName() APIs
item.description:
Custom spans in Workers now support three more methods from the OpenTelemetry span API.

  • span.spanContext() returns the span's traceId, spanId, and traceFlags. The IDs match the trace and span IDs in Workers Observability and in exported traces, so you can log them or return them to clients to correlate a request with its trace.
  • span.setStatus(status) sets the span status to "unset", "ok", or "error", with an optional message for errors. Span status is included in traces exported to OpenTelemetry destinations. The Workers Observability dashboard does not display it yet.
  • span.updateName(name) renames a span after it starts, such as once you know which route a request matched. You can also rename the invocation's root span returned by tracing.getActiveSpan().

For more details, refer to the custom spans documentation.

item.title: D1 - D1 database undelete requests limited to the last 7 days
item.description:
The D1 undelete API now only accepts requests for databases that were deleted within the last 7 days. Requests to undelete a database that was deleted more than 7 days ago will fail and return an error.

If you delete a D1 database by mistake, send the undelete request as soon as possible, and no later than 7 days after deletion.

For more information, refer to the undelete D1 database API reference.

item.title: Flagship - Target Flagship feature flags with structured evaluation context
item.description:
Flagship supports nested objects, arrays, and null in evaluation context. Pass user profiles and tag lists directly, then target nested attributes without flattening your application data.

For example, pass a profile and tags when evaluating a flag through the Workers binding:

A targeting rule can combine profile.plan equals "enterprise" with tags has "beta" to serve the feature to enterprise users in the beta group. Use dot-separated paths for nested attributes and the has and not_has operators for array membership. Percentage rollouts can also use a nested identifier, such as profile.id, for consistent user assignment.

Structured context works through the Workers binding, the evaluation REST API with a JSON POST body, and the TypeScript, Python, and Go OpenFeature SDKs from version 0.6.0. The SDKs automatically use POST when HTTP evaluation requires structured context.

Refer to targeting rules, the evaluation API, and SDK context support for usage and supported values.

item.title: Workers, Pages - Workers Builds and Pages build images reject compromised eMudhra certificates
item.description:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. The Workers Builds and Pages build images now reject these certificates when your build clones your repository, installs dependencies, or makes HTTPS requests.

The updated images include patched CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4 and 24.22.1, Bun 1.4.4, and pip 26.2.2. Build commands also run with environment variables that point older runtimes at the patched CA certificates.

What you need to do

Most projects need no changes. Update your project if:

  • You set BUN_VERSION below 1.4.4. Older Bun versions trust the compromised certificates.
  • You set your own SSL_CERT_FILE, PIP_CERT, or REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, or set --use-bundled-ca in NODE_OPTIONS. Make sure your CA certificates do not trust the compromised intermediates.
  • Your build installs tools that ship their own CA certificates. Update them to a version that removes the compromised intermediates.

For details, refer to the build image documentation for Workers Builds and Pages.

item.title: Workers - Pin your npm version in Workers Builds with packageManager
item.description:
You can now choose the npm version that Workers Builds uses by setting the packageManager field in your package.json. Before the build installs dependencies, it installs the npm version you set, so a lockfile written by a newer npm version installs the same way in your build as it does locally.

The packageManager field also sets the version of Yarn, pnpm, and Bun. Use an exact version, such as npm@11.19.1, not a range. Workers Builds does not use the engines.npm field to choose an npm version.

For more information, refer to Package manager versions.

item.title: Agents - Cloudflare MCP servers no longer serve /sse
item.description:
Cloudflare's product-specific MCP servers now serve only /mcp. A request to /sse returns 410 Gone with the server's /mcp URL, which most MCP clients show in their connection error.

If your MCP client is configured with an /sse URL, change it to /mcp, for example https://docs.mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. If you signed in through /sse, your client asks you to sign in again. Connections that already use /mcp are not affected.

item.title: Agents - Agents SDK now supports the latest Pi 1.4 release
item.description:
Agents SDK v0.30.0 runs PiHarness on Pi 1.4 ↗︎, and makes it recover more reliably from evictions, crashes, and storage errors.

  • Hibernation while Pi's tasks sleep. PiHarness passes Pi's new onWake callback to your harness factory. While a task sleeps, such as during a model retry backoff, the Durable Object can hibernate until the task is due instead of staying in memory.
  • Parked tasks. Pi 1.4 parks a task that keeps crashing the object instead of restarting it forever. Parked operations show as parked in pending(), and session.retry() runs them again.
  • Recovery from storage errors. PiHarness reopens Pi after a storage error instead of failing every call until the object restarts. Its wake-up job retries failed steps with a backoff instead of being dropped.
  • Retried model streams. agents/models/pi-ai reports a cut-off or idle model stream as a transient error, so Pi retries the turn instead of failing it.

Upgrade

The Agents SDK v0.30.0 changelog ↗︎ has step-by-step upgrade instructions. Point your coding agent at them and upgrade today:

Pi 1.4 migrates the session storage in the object's SQLite database to a schema that Pi 1.3 cannot open, so a deployment cannot roll back past this upgrade. Refer to the Pi Durable 1.4.0 changelog ↗︎ for Pi's own breaking changes.

item.title: Sandboxes - Sandbox SDK 0.12.14 updates trusted certificates after the eMudhra compromise
item.description:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities ↗︎ can be recovered, so anyone can forge a certificate for any hostname that chains to them. Sandbox SDK images before 0.12.14 trust these certificates. An HTTPS connection that leaves the container directly, such as one from mountBucket(), backups, gitCheckout(), tunnels, or code that runs in the sandbox, can be intercepted with a forged certificate.

What you need to do

Sandbox SDK 0.x

Update immediately. Install @cloudflare/sandbox@0.12.14, change the FROM line in your Dockerfile to the matching image, and redeploy. Keep any -python, -opencode, or -musl suffix on the image tag. The deployment's rollout replaces running sandboxes with ones that use the new image.

If you use the next prerelease, update to 0.13.0-next.825.1 or later.

If you cannot update yet and use 0.8.7 or later, send all HTTPS through your Worker, so that Cloudflare checks every certificate on port 443 whatever your image trusts:

Deploy, then stop running sandboxes so that they restart with the interception certificate. This does not cover TLS on other ports, such as cloudflared tunnels, and clients that ignore the injected certificate fail to connect. For more information, refer to HTTPS traffic.

Sandbox SDK 1.x

You do not need to update the SDK, because it makes no TLS connections of its own. Your image decides which certificates your sandboxes trust, so rebuild it and replace the sandboxes that run the old one:

  1. Run docker pull for each base image in your Dockerfile, then clear the Docker build cache with docker builder prune --all. wrangler deploy builds with your local images and build cache, so without these steps it can ship the old CA certificates and runtimes. If your Wrangler configuration references an image by digest, build and push a new image and update the digest instead.
  2. Deploy your Worker.
  3. Stop sandboxes that are still running, for example with this.ctx.container.destroy(). A running sandbox keeps the image it started with until it stops. To restart only the sandboxes whose image is out of date, refer to Roll out a named image update.
  4. If you use snapshots, create new ones from sandboxes that run the updated image. A snapshot restores the image it was created from, so an older snapshot brings back the old certificates.

Check your sandboxes

From inside a sandbox, connect to one of the test hosts listed at emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com ↗︎ with each TLS client your code uses, such as curl, node, or bun. Every request should fail:

What changed in 0.12.13 and 0.12.14

In the 0.12.13 images, the system CA bundle, Node.js, cloudflared, and pip reject certificates from the compromised intermediates. The images ship updated Ubuntu and Alpine CA certificates, Node.js 22.23.4, cloudflared 2026.10.2, and pip 26.2.2 in the -python image.

0.12.14 updates Bun to 1.4.4, so the bun command and createBackup() uploads of archives of 10 MiB or more reject these certificates too. The -opencode image ships OpenCode 1.19.4 or later, which also runs on Bun 1.4.4.

item.title: Agents, Workers AI, AI Gateway - createAI replaces workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider
item.description:
The Agents SDK has a new createAI function for the AI SDK and Pi AI. It unifies what workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider did: Workers AI models, AI Gateway catalog models, dynamic routes, and vendor models, through the AI binding or an account id and API token.

workers-ai-provider and ai-gateway-provider are now feature frozen and marked as deprecated. Please migrate at your convenience.

With createAI you get:

  • Every model by id. Workers AI @cf/ ids, any model in the AI Gateway catalog, and dynamic routes as dynamic/<route>.
  • Vendor model objects. Pass a model from the vendor's own package, such as ai(anthropic("claude-opus-5-5")). It goes unchanged to AI Gateway's provider-native endpoint.
  • The binding, or an account id and API token. Use a gateway in another account, or call from outside a Worker.
  • Gateway options, fallback, and BYOK. Caching, logging, metadata, retries, byokAlias, zdr, and vendorKey.
  • Stream resume. Through the binding, a catalog or dynamic route stream that drops mid-answer resumes.
  • Other model types. Embeddings, images, speech, transcription, and reranking in the AI SDK provider, and images in Pi AI.
Before After
createWorkersAI({ binding }) createAI({ binding })
createWorkersAI({ accountId, apiKey }) createAI({ accountId, apiToken })
createAiGateway(...) createAI(...), with fallback for a list of models
createAISearch from workers-ai-provider createAISearchNamespace from ai-search-provider

For AI Search, use ai-search-provider. For more information, refer to Models.

item.title: Basin SQL, Basin - Basin SQL supports OFFSET
item.description:
Basin SQL is a serverless, distributed SQL engine for querying Apache Iceberg tables in Basin Catalog. It now supports OFFSET, which lets you skip a specified number of rows when retrieving query results.

Use LIMIT to set the page size and OFFSET to skip earlier rows. With a page size of 100, use OFFSET 0 for the first page, OFFSET 100 for the second, and increase the offset by 100 for each later page. Add ORDER BY on a unique column to keep the row order consistent.

For example, this query returns the second page of 100 rows:

For syntax and examples, refer to the OFFSET clause in the Basin SQL reference.

item.title: Agents, Workers - Think agents now use a @cloudflare/computer workspace
item.description:
Think and Agent Skills now use the workspace from @cloudflare/computer ↗︎ as well as the filesystem tools. A JavaScript execution environment can be configured by adding the WorkerJavaScriptBackend.

@cloudflare/shell is deprecated, and so is Think's createExecuteTool. These will no longer be developed nor supported from today onwards.

Migrate your workspace data

This is a breaking change. @cloudflare/computer stores files in different tables from @cloudflare/shell, and there is no automatic data migration between workspace formats. To keep an existing workspace, copy its files with the script in Migrating from @cloudflare/shell to @cloudflare/computer ↗︎. Otherwise your agent will start with an empty workspace, though the original data will still be present in the existing tables.

For more information, refer to Think tools.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Wrangler and cf now upload source maps by default
item.description:
From Wrangler 4.150.0, wrangler deploy, wrangler versions upload, and wrangler preview generate and upload source maps by default. You no longer need to set upload_source_maps to get stack traces with your original file names and line numbers.

cf deploy also uploads source maps by default. With the Cloudflare Vite plugin 1.64.0 or later, Worker builds generate source maps by default, and cf deploy uploads every source map in the build output.

Remapped stack traces show up in Workers Logs, real-time logs, Tail Workers, and Workers Issues. Source maps are applied after your Worker runs, so they don't affect CPU time, bundle size, or cold starts.

If your Worker uses a custom build, Wrangler uploads any external source maps it finds. Maps it can't resolve, such as inline data: source maps, are skipped instead of failing the upload. Set upload_source_maps to true if you'd prefer the upload to fail.

To opt out with Wrangler, set upload_source_maps to false:

To opt out with cf or the Cloudflare Vite plugin, set build.sourcemap to false for your Worker's Vite environment. Refer to Disable source maps.

item.title: Agents - Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization
item.description:
The Cloudflare API MCP server now supports step-up authorization ↗︎.

Grant only the required scopes when you connect, then authorize more on demand as your agent performs a task. When a tool call needs a scope you have not granted, the server returns an insufficient_scope challenge ↗︎ naming it, and your MCP client asks you to approve it. Scopes you already granted are kept.

To start with the least access, choose Minimal on the consent page when you connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. Refer to authorization in MCP.

Available now in all MCP clients that support step-up authorization.

item.title: Workers AI - Introducing Clairic: an extraction model for typed values, now on Workers AI
item.description:
@cf/cloudflare/clairic is now available on Workers AI as a preview. Clairic is the first extraction model: a System One model that answers with values instead of text. We intend to release the model with open weights soon.

Decision models such as Clef choose among options you define up front. Many structured-output tasks do not have answers you can list in advance: an invoice total, a delivery date, the number of days a shipment is late, or what a repair will cost. Clairic handles these. You send a state and a schema of typed fields, and it returns one typed value per field. A value is read from the input, computed from it, or predicted beyond it.

Clairic does not generate tokens. It reads your input in one pass and decodes each answer under the rules of its type, so every answer is a valid value of the type you asked for, or null when the input does not determine it.

Typed fields

Define as many fields as you need. Fields that do not fit beside the input in one pass are split across parallel passes, so there is no upper limit.

Type Returns
text An exact span of the input, with its character offsets
number A number read or worked out from the input, honoring integer and decimals
date, time, datetime Real calendar dates and valid times, in ISO form
duration A length of time in the unit you choose
list Every matching text, number, or date, in input order
estimate A distribution inside your min and max, on your step grid, on a linear or log scale
forecast One estimate per future step of a series, up to 64 steps

Every scalar answer includes p_null, the probability that the input does not determine the value, and a confidence score. Estimates and forecasts include a median and an 80% interval (p10 to p90). Set options.include_quantiles to also get all 99 percentiles. Use these to decide what to automate and what to send to review.

You can also pass up to four images alongside the state.

Preview

The current endpoint is an early checkpoint, and we expect it to improve:

  • Arithmetic: One- and two-step calculations, such as totals, differences, conversions, and date arithmetic, are reliable. Long chains of dependent steps and aggregations across many table rows are not yet. Extract the inputs with Clairic and do the math in code.
  • Estimates: Clairic estimates best when the input contains evidence such as comparables, history, or descriptive text. Without evidence, the interval is wide.
  • Forecasts: Forecasting is basic. Next-step forecasts follow recent patterns, but forecasts several steps out flatten toward the average, and Clairic does not anticipate events the series does not show, such as holidays. It does not replace a time-series model trained on your data.
  • Calibration: Intervals are trained to be calibrated and are on most held-out sets, but they can run narrow on unfamiliar data.
  • Confidence: Every answer is well formed, not necessarily correct. Use confidence, p_null, and the intervals to decide what to automate and what to send to review.
  • Dates: Dates without a year are resolved from context. If a field depends on the current date, set reference_date or add a line such as Today: 2026-10-19 to the state.

Pricing

Clairic costs $0.10 per million input tokens. Because it generates no tokens, there is no output token charge.

Get started

Use Clairic through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clairic model page, extraction models, pricing, and the blog post ↗︎.

item.title: Workers AI - DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 now available on Workers AI
item.description:
@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017 is now available on Workers AI. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 552B backbone parameters. It activates 8B parameters per token during prefill and 16B during decode, which keeps input-heavy agentic workloads fast and low-cost.

The 1017 release is an update to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks, and it completes tasks with shorter outputs.

Key capabilities:

  • Vision: Send images alongside text in the same request.
  • Reasoning: Reasoning is on by default at high effort. Set reasoning_effort to low or max to change the effort, or to none to turn reasoning off.
  • Function calling: Build agents that invoke tools and APIs across multiple conversation turns.
  • Long context: A full 1,048,576 token context window.

DeepSeek V4.1 Flash requires the Workers Paid plan or prepaid AI Gateway credits. The default rate limit is 20 requests per minute with standard Workers AI billing and 50 requests per minute with prepaid AI Gateway credits. For details, refer to limits.

Use DeepSeek V4.1 Flash through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()), the REST API, the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or AI Gateway.

For more information, refer to the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash model page and pricing.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Test Cron Triggers with Local Explorer
item.description:
Local Explorer can now send one-off Cron Trigger invocations to a Worker's scheduled() handler during local development. This removes the need to construct request URLs when testing handler behavior.

Start your local development server with cf dev, wrangler dev, or the Cloudflare Vite plugin. Open /cdn-cgi/local/explorer on the server URL and select Cron Triggers.

The browser interface supports the following tasks:

  • Invoke configured cron expressions
  • Build ad hoc expressions
  • Set reusable scheduled times
  • Inspect outcomes and noRetry() status

Ad hoc triggers and scheduled time presets stay in your browser. They do not change cloudflare.config.ts, your Wrangler configuration, or deployed Cron Triggers. Local development does not run cron schedules automatically.

Full logs and traces are available in the development session that owns the Worker when that session has Observability turned on.

The following example uses port 8787. Replace it with your development server port, such as 5173 for Vite.

The Local Explorer API exposes the same operation for tools and AI agents. The request targets an exact Worker name and accepts a cron expression and optional scheduled time:

For more details, refer to Test Cron Triggers with Local Explorer.

item.title: AI Search - AI Search keyword search supports Japanese, Chinese, and Korean queries
item.description:
AI Search keyword search with the trigram tokenizer now matches Japanese, Chinese, and Korean queries, including full natural-language questions such as 経費精算の締め日はいつですか？. Previously, a query without spaces was treated as a single exact phrase and usually returned no keyword results.

The porter tokenizer does not work well for these languages. If your content is in Japanese, Chinese, or Korean, set keyword_tokenizer to trigram. Changing the tokenizer triggers a full reindex.

Refer to Keyword search for tokenizer details.

item.title: Workers, Cloudflare CLI - Search Cloudflare documentation with the Cloudflare CLI
item.description:
Cloudflare CLI 1.0.0-beta.16 includes cf docs search, so you and your coding agent can find Cloudflare documentation without leaving the terminal. Search for guides, tutorials, and examples across Cloudflare products.

To install or update to the latest release:

npm install --global cf@latest
yarn global add cf@latest
pnpm add --global cf@latest
bun add --global cf@latest

Describe what you want to do, or ask a question:

The command searches live Cloudflare documentation and returns up to five ranked JSON results. Each result includes a title, description, and documentation URL. An Internet connection is required.

Agents can parse the results and fetch a complete page as Markdown. For example, use jq to select the first result, then request its URL with the Accept: text/markdown header:

This release also standardizes generated command names to kebab-case. For example, cf accounts billing getCredits becomes cf accounts billing get-credits. For the full list of breaking command and flag changes, refer to the Cloudflare CLI release notes ↗︎.

For more information, refer to Find Cloudflare documentation with a coding agent.

item.title: Cloudflare One, Workers, Gateway - Gateway and Workers integration is now in public beta
item.description:
Cloudflare Gateway now integrates with Cloudflare Workers in public beta on all Zero Trust plans. You can use the Forward action in Gateway HTTP policies to run your own code on matching, permitted traffic without managing a separate proxy.

The Forward action lets you transform HTTP requests and responses, return a coaching page, or run background tasks such as Slack notifications and R2 captures. Your Worker receives the request and Gateway context, including connection metadata, user identity, and device posture when available.

Gateway handles the proxy connection, TLS decryption, and upstream routing. It evaluates HTTP request policies before Forward policies and inspects the final response before returning it to the user.

Gateway inspects the original request body before delivering it to your Worker. A body-inspection Block decision can interrupt the Worker.

To get started, deploy a Worker and configure a Forward policy, or adapt one of the Worker templates.

item.title: Stream - Ultra-low latency live with WebRTC is now Generally Available in Stream
item.description:
Stream WebRTC support lets you deliver high quality live video to thousands of concurrent viewers in milliseconds. WebRTC is compatible with native Web APIs and standard protocols, so creators can go live from a browser without needing a separate broadcast application. This powers platforms to build custom experiences with deep feature integration for creators as well as viewers. Here's how to get started with a Stream live input and a browser.

Usage-based billing for WebRTC begins today, October 15, 2026 and follows the standard rates for minutes of video delivered. Refer to pricing ↗︎ for rates.

What changed

While in beta, Stream’s WebRTC support was rebuilt from the ground up to leverage Cloudflare Realtime ↗︎’s primitives for stability and scale while managing these components in Stream’s familiar, unified API that makes it easy to build. We also adopted the latest WHIP and WHEP protocol standards for Trickle ICE, server and client offer modes, and counter-offer support for improved player library compatibility and network traversal adaptability. Finally, WebRTC delivery will now be visible in Stream’s analytics ↗︎ and billable usage charts.

How does this relate to Cloudflare Realtime

Realtime exposes a set of tools and primitives to build applications that connect people, AI systems, and devices together in many-to-many experiences powered by WebRTC. Stream leverages these building-blocks to deliver one-to-many broadcast capabilities, controlled and managed by a single, unified API with features like the built-in player ↗︎ and analytics ↗︎ that make it easy to get started.

How do I get started

First, create a live input ↗︎ using cf ↗︎, the API, or in the Stream Dashboard ↗︎:

The response will include webRTC and webRTCPlayback properties, each containing a url for WHIP (broadcast) and WHEP (playback) respectively.

Next, you can go live using WHIP directly from a browser or supported broadcast software. Refer to our new tutorial ↗︎ that shows a dependency-free way to broadcast live video with browser-native JavaScript.

Finally, you can play using WHEP using Stream’s built-in player ↗︎, a supported player app/library, or simple JavaScript:

Learn more in the Stream WebRTC docs or try the all-in-one tutorial for yourself.

item.title: Workers AI, Realtime - Pipecat PhoneLLM Mini now available on Workers AI
item.description:
@cf/daily-co/phonellm-mini-alpha-2, a model from the Pipecat ↗︎ team at Daily, is now available on Workers AI. PhoneLLM is built for voice agents and other realtime AI applications, where a model has to reply quickly and call the right tool mid-conversation.

In a voice agent, the language model sits between speech-to-text and text-to-speech, so every second it takes adds to the caller's wait. Developers usually choose between a fast model without reasoning mode, which can miss instructions or tool calls, and a slower model in reasoning mode, which handles both well. Pipecat post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano 30B on phone and customer support scenarios so PhoneLLM follows instructions and calls tools better without reasoning mode.

You can use PhoneLLM through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. Pipecat recommends temperature: 0. Also set chat_template_kwargs: { enable_thinking: false }.

Run a voice agent with Pipecat on Workers

Pipecat ↗︎ is an open-source Python framework for building voice agents. Now that Python Workers are generally available, you can run a Pipecat voice agent on Cloudflare.

Our Pipecat voice agent example ↗︎ runs in a Durable Object and uses WebRTC as the voice transport through the Realtime SFU. It uses DeepSeek V4 Flash by default. To deploy it with PhoneLLM, give this prompt to your coding agent:

For more information, refer to the PhoneLLM Mini model page, Pipecat's model card ↗︎, and Workers AI pricing.

item.title: Workers - Workers Builds now uses newer versions of Node.js, Python, Go, Bun, and more
item.description:
Your builds now run on newer versions of Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, Bun, Yarn, and Python package managers by default, so you get the latest fixes and features without changing your build configuration.

Runtimes

Runtime Previous version New version Override with
Node.js 24.18.0 24.21.0 NODE_VERSION
Python 3.13.3 3.14.8 PYTHON_VERSION
Ruby 3.4.7 3.4.11 RUBY_VERSION
Go 1.24.3 1.27.2 GO_VERSION

Tools and package managers

Tool Previous version New version Override with
Bun 1.2.15 1.4.3 BUN_VERSION
Yarn 4.9.1 4.18.1 YARN_VERSION
pip 25.1.1 26.2.1
pipx 1.7.1 1.17.2
Poetry 2.1.3 2.4.3
uv 0.7.13 0.12.10

Bun 1.4.3 supports both v1 (bun.lockb) and v2 (bun.lock) lockfiles, so existing Bun projects continue to install without changes.

If your project already sets a version through an environment variable or a version file (such as .nvmrc, .node-version, .python-version, or .ruby-version), your builds continue to use that version. To keep using a previous default, add the matching environment variable to your build configuration. For example, set PYTHON_VERSION to 3.13.3.

For more information, refer to Override default versions and the build image policy.

item.title: Agents, Workers - Cloudflare API MCP server sends Workers Issues as MCP Events
item.description:
Workers Issues provides built-in error monitoring for Cloudflare Workers. It detects production failures and groups related failures into issues without an SDK or application wrapper.

The Cloudflare API MCP server now sends these issues as MCP Events ↗︎, the first event it exposes. MCP clients discover cloudflare.alert.workers_observability_real_time_issue with events/list and subscribe with events/subscribe, scoped to an account or a single Worker. When Issues detects a new or recurring issue, the server posts a signed event to the client's webhook, so an agent can start investigating without polling.

To use it, enable Issues on your Worker and connect https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp with the Notifications Write and Workers Observability Write permissions to a client that supports MCP Events webhooks.

item.title: Agents - New persistent browser tool in the Agents SDK, with tabs and logins that last between turns
item.description:
The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a browserTool that gives your agent a Browser Run browser it can return to on later turns. Your agent can open a website, inspect a page, and come back to it with its tabs, cookies, and login session intact while the browser session remains alive.

When you give browserTool to your agent, the model writes code that drives the browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP). Screenshots return as images that an image-capable model can inspect and your UI can display.

To use browserTool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.28.0 ↗︎ or greater installed. Create a Browser, register it with your object's Lifecycle, and add the tool to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

Each Pi conversation gets its own active tab by default. Cookies and logins remain shared within the browser.

The browser stays alive between turns, including when the Durable Object hibernates. Its default idle timeout is 10 minutes. If the session expires or crashes, the tool creates a fresh browser and reports restarted: true. The old tabs and login state are gone.

You can also use the persistent browser with the AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters, or connect another harness through the public Browser and CDP APIs.

Refer to persistent browser tools for the complete Pi Durable example, required bindings, and behavior when a tool call is interrupted.

item.title: Agents - New web_fetch tool in the Agents SDK for reading webpages and documents, with automatic markdown conversion
item.description:
The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a web_fetch tool that reads webpages, PDFs, and supported Office documents, using Workers AI Markdown Conversion to turn them into text the model can read. The tool requests Markdown directly from sites that support Markdown for Agents and formats JSON for the model.

When you give the web_fetch tool to your agent, the model provides a URL and receives back the page content, along with the final URL, HTTP status, and content type. Long pages come back in smaller sections, with an offset the model can use to continue reading. You control which hosts the agent can fetch, response size, timeouts, and redirects.

When you also provide the web_search tool to your agent, the model is told to use web_fetch to read the pages that web_search returns.

To use the web_fetch tool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.28.0 ↗︎ or greater installed, and add it to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

The web_fetch tool works with any harness. The SDK includes AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters. If you use a different harness, or need to fetch a page without calling a model, use fetchWeb(), windowWebFetchPage(), and renderWebFetchPage() from agents/webfetch. Direct fetching does not require a Durable Object or browser.

For setup, examples, and request controls, refer to Web fetch.

item.title: Agents, Workers - Run OpenCode 2.0 on Cloudflare with the Agents SDK
item.description:
The Agents SDK now supports OpenCode 2.0 ↗︎ through the experimental OpenCodeHarness. Run OpenCode inside a plain Durable Object, with sessions stored in SQLite and Lifecycle jobs that wake interrupted work after eviction.

The agents/models/opencode provider connects OpenCode to Workers AI through the AI binding. OpenCode plugins extend the harness with custom tools, remote MCP servers, and skills. Refer to OpenCode's Cloudflare SDK documentation ↗︎ for the embedded host API.

Install Agents SDK 0.28.0 or later with the OpenCode packages:

npm i agents@latest @opencode/sdk@2 @opencode/plugin@2
yarn add agents@latest @opencode/sdk@2 @opencode/plugin@2
pnpm add agents@latest @opencode/sdk@2 @opencode/plugin@2
bun add agents@latest @opencode/sdk@2 @opencode/plugin@2

Create a harness and install a Lifecycle on your Durable Object:

The OpenCode harness guide includes the workerTools plugin, Wrangler configuration, and session APIs. The working example ↗︎ adds a browser UI, WebSocket streaming, and Workspace tools from @cloudflare/computer for files and code execution.

item.title: Agents - New web_search tool in the Agents SDK, powered by the Cloudflare Web Search API
item.description:
The Cloudflare Agents SDK now provides a web_search tool that searches the public web through the Cloudflare Web Search API, powered by ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup.

When you give the web_search tool to your agent, the model provides a query and max results, and receives back a short numbered list of titles, URLs, and trimmed descriptions. When you also provide the web_fetch tool to your agent, the model is told to use it to read the pages that the web_search tool returns.

To use the web_search tool, make sure you have Agents SDK v0.27.0 ↗︎ or greater installed, and add it to a Pi Durable extension registry before opening the harness:

The SDK also includes AI SDK and TanStack AI adapters. To search without a model, such as from a scheduled job, use createAIWebSearch() or createHTTPWebSearch() from agents/websearch.

For setup, options, and error handling, refer to Web search.

item.title: Queues - Queues now supports EU, US, and FedRAMP jurisdictions
item.description:
You can now create Cloudflare Queues with jurisdictional restrictions, ensuring that messages published to a queue are stored and processed only within a specific jurisdiction. This helps you comply with data residency requirements such as the GDPR ↗︎ or FedRAMP ↗︎.

To create a jurisdiction-restricted queue with the Cloudflare CLI (cf), use the --jurisdiction flag:

You can also pass a jurisdiction parameter when calling the Create Queue endpoint:

Supported jurisdictions are eu (European Union), us (United States), and fedramp (FedRAMP-Moderate data centers). Jurisdiction can only be set when a queue is created and cannot be changed afterwards.

For more information, refer to Queues data location.

item.title: Workers - Workers Builds now posts preview URLs in seconds
item.description:
Workers Builds now consistently posts preview URLs to GitHub pull requests and GitLab merge requests within a few seconds of a build completing, so you can start testing and reviewing your changes sooner. Previously, posting preview URLs could often take minutes.

For details, refer to Workers Builds GitHub integration and Workers Builds GitLab integration.

item.title: Workers - More time for requests to finish during Workers runtime updates
item.description:
Pending requests and connections to Workers now have a grace period of up to 20 minutes during Workers runtime updates. Previously, the grace period was up to 30 seconds.

This gives long-running HTTP requests, streamed AI responses, and live WebSocket sessions more time to continue before an update interrupts them.

New incoming HTTP requests go to the updated version of the Workers runtime once it is ready. Processes running the previous version stop accepting these requests and drain existing work. The grace period applies to each process running the previous version. When it ends, unfinished requests and open connections on that process are terminated.

You should design your application to reconnect WebSockets, safely retry interrupted requests, and recover saved state after a restart. WebSockets can disconnect before the grace period ends, including connections using the WebSocket Hibernation API.

For more information, refer to Workers runtime updates.

item.title: Agents - Cloudflare API MCP server serves Cloudflare skills
item.description:
The Cloudflare API MCP server now serves Cloudflare skills ↗︎ through the Skills over MCP extension ↗︎. MCP clients that support the extension discover the skills with skills/list and read their files at skill://<name>/<path>.

To use them, add https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp to an MCP client that supports the extension ↗︎.

item.title: R2 - R2 bandwidth by Cloudflare location
item.description:
You can now view R2 bandwidth by the Cloudflare location that served each request in the Cloudflare UI. This helps you see which locations consume the most bandwidth with options to select a specific bucket and download (read) vs upload (write) bandwidth.

Go to R2 overview ↗

By default, the chart shows the top five locations by total bandwidth consumed during the selected time range. Use the Top 5 locations dropdown to select other locations, up to six at a time.

For more information, refer to R2 metrics and analytics.

item.title: Workers AI - Clef-omni adds audio and video input, Clef-flash is now cheaper, and Clef is faster
item.description:
@cf/cloudflare/clef-omni is now available on Workers AI. Clef-omni is a decision model that takes audio (WAV or MP3) and video (MP4 or WebM) input alongside text and images. It joins Clef and Clef-flash in the Clef family of open-weight decision models. We also cut the price of Clef-flash, so it now costs less than Jev, and made Clef faster.

Clef-omni: one decision model for every modality

Previously, making a decision about a voice recording or a video meant chaining models together: transcribe the speech, split the audio and visual tracks, then pass the results to a text decision model. Clef-omni reads every modality directly in one request. A video's soundtrack is aligned with its frames, so the model can reason over what is seen and heard at the same time.

Clef-omni is built on a 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) backbone with 3B active parameters. Like the rest of the Clef family, it does not generate text. It scores every allowed answer in a single pass, so decisions return quickly:

  • Text requests: about 20 ms
  • Image or audio inputs: under 100 ms
  • A 21-second video clip with sound: about 300 ms

Pass media as base64 data URLs in the images, audio, and videos fields:

Clef-omni scores highest of the Clef family on BANKING77, CLINC150+OOS, and Amazon ESCI:

Benchmark Clef-omni Clef Clef-flash Jev
BFCL (case exact) 98.2 98.47 98.76 95.75
BANKING77 (macro-F1) 94.8 94.20 90.93 79.74
CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1) 97.7 97.43 66.77 89.27
Amazon ESCI (macro-F1) 57.8 57.48 57.39 55.21
PhishNChips (accuracy) 73.2 79.60 75.05 62.55

Clef-flash is now cheaper

Clef-flash now costs $0.038 per million input tokens, down from $0.090, which makes it cheaper than Jev. To offer this price, the hosted Clef-flash context window is now 24K tokens, down from 64K. Based on usage data, only 0.24% of requests exceed 24K input tokens. If you need a larger context window, use Clef, which keeps its 64K context window.

The Clef-flash weights on Hugging Face are unchanged and support up to a 256K context window if you self-host.

Model Price Context window
@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash $0.038 per M input tokens 24K tokens
@cf/cloudflare/clef $0.240 per M input tokens 64K tokens
@cf/cloudflare/clef-omni $0.150 per M input tokens 64K tokens

All Clef models convert image inputs to input tokens, and Clef-omni does the same for audio and video. For details on how each input type is tokenized, refer to the Clef, Clef-flash, and Clef-omni model pages.

Clef is now faster

We optimized how Clef is served on Workers AI, so it now returns decisions up to 2x faster. The model weights are unchanged.

Input size Before: median / p95 (ms) Now: median / p95 (ms) Median speedup
~800 tokens 262 / 438 152 / 351 1.7x
~3,400 tokens 616 / 777 305 / 531 2.0x
~16,000 tokens 2,721 / 3,250 1,635 / 1,805 1.7x

Part of this speedup comes from moving Clef to SGLang ↗︎. Clef support is coming to SGLang in version 0.5.22 (PR #42721 ↗︎). If you self-host Clef, launch commands are available in the Clef collection on Hugging Face ↗︎.

Get started

Clef-omni follows the same System One API as Clef and Clef-flash, and works with AI Gateway. To try it, change the model ID to @cf/cloudflare/clef-omni and set the model selector to clef-omni.

For more information, refer to the Clef-omni model page and pricing.

item.title: Workflows, Workers - Create Workflow instance batches by count or list
item.description:
createBatch() now accepts an options object that creates up to 100 Workflow instances in one call. The result lists the created instances and explains why any others were not created. To use this form in local development and get its types from wrangler types, use Wrangler 4.148.0 or later.

To create instances that share the same options, pass count. Each instance receives a generated ID:

To give each instance its own ID or options, pass instances:

created contains the created instances. errors contains each entry that was not created, identified by its position in the input. IDs that already exist and IDs repeated within the batch are reported as errors instead of being skipped silently.

Passing an array to createBatch() is deprecated. Existing code that uses the array form continues to work.

For more information, refer to createBatch.

item.title: AI Gateway - AI Gateway log IDs and request IDs now use UUIDv7
item.description:
New AI Gateway log IDs and request IDs are lowercase UUIDv7, such as 019a7b3e-5f2c-7c41-9d3e-2b8f6a1c4e07. Previously, log IDs were 26-character ULIDs and request IDs were random UUIDs.

For a request that AI Gateway answers in a single step, the cf-aig-request-id, cf-aig-log-id, and cf-aig-event-id response headers now carry the same value. For provider and Universal requests, if you set your own cf-aig-event-id, AI Gateway returns it instead.

Existing log IDs do not change, and the logs API accepts both formats. Treat log IDs as opaque strings, and update any code that checks for the ULID format.

item.title: AI Gateway - Standardize provider credential error responses in AI Gateway
item.description:
AI Gateway's REST API now returns consistent responses when an AI provider rejects credentials. The change applies to POST /ai/run ↗︎.

Scenario Previous AI Gateway response New AI Gateway response
ElevenLabs Provider-specific UserCredentialsError with HTTP 403 HTTP 401 with error code 2009
Google Vertex HTTP 500 for rejected credentials, with upstream retries HTTP 401 with error code 2009; the request fails without retrying the provider
All other providers HTTP 402 or another provider-specific status for rejected credentials HTTP 401 with error code 2009
When using Unified Billing, the provider rejects the credentials Provider-specific authentication error HTTP 503

Update applications that handle AI Gateway REST API errors to treat HTTP 401 as an invalid or rejected provider credential.

For details about providing provider credentials, refer to Bring your own provider keys.

item.title: AI Gateway, Web Search API - Introducing Web Search API
item.description:
Web Search API is now available in beta. Web Search API lets your AI agents and applications search the Internet and ground their responses in live information, instead of guessing URLs or relying on a model's training cutoff.

At launch, you can choose between three search providers: Ceramic.ai, Exa, and Linkup. All three support Zero Data Retention for requests made through Cloudflare, and all have committed to Cloudflare's verified bot crawling standards.

Web Search API runs through AI Gateway, so search requests appear in your gateway logs and are billed to your AI Gateway credits at each provider's list API price, with no additional markup. You can also bring your own provider API key.

Call Web Search API with the REST API:

Or from a Worker with the AI binding:

To get started, refer to How to use Web Search API.

item.title: Agents, Workers - Run the Pi Durable harness on Cloudflare with the Agents SDK
item.description:
The Agents SDK now provides first-class support for building agents using the Pi harness. You can build long-running agents using the combination of Pi 1.0 ↗︎, Pi Durable ↗︎, and the new PiHarness class that the Cloudflare Agents SDK provides, ensuring your agent's work is durably persisted, even if interrupted mid-turn.

Built with Earendil ↗︎, this integration is our first step toward first-class support for third-party agent harnesses on Cloudflare.

Beta

PiHarness is in beta. Pi Durable ↗︎ is a new, experimental package, and the PiHarness API will likely change as Pi Durable matures.

PiHarness is a new "Lifecycle capability" provided by the Cloudflare Agents SDK. Pi Durable provides the agent harness and the Lifecycle is responsible for keeping the agent running in the Durable Object. The Lifecycle is a core concept in the Agents SDK ensuring that long-running work can run in a Durable Object, surviving restarts, crashes, and network issues. We will share more on Lifecycle capabilities in the near future.

Install

npm i agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
yarn add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
pnpm add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai
bun add agents@latest @earendil-works/pi-durable @earendil-works/pi-ai

Both Pi packages are optional peer dependencies of agents, so you only install them if you use the harness.

Use it in an Agent

Creating a Pi agent requires configuring the Pi Harness with a model, skills, and tools, then registering the PiHarness with the Agent class.

The agents/models/pi-ai entry point supports AI Gateway and Workers AI models, so you can get started with Cloudflare models right away or use your existing Pi AI provider.

Add tools with extensions

Both tools and system prompt sections are provided to the Pi Harness via extensions.

For more information on creating and configuring extensions, refer to Extensions.

Learn more

  • Pi harness documentation
  • Pi harness extensions
  • pi-ai model provider
  • Pi harness example ↗︎, with WebSockets, a browser UI, and a @cloudflare/computer Workspace for the model's tools
  • Lifecycle ↗︎
  • Pi Durable announcement ↗︎ from Earendil

item.title: D1 - United States jurisdiction
item.description:
You can create D1 databases with the us jurisdiction. These databases run and persist data within the United States.

Use this option for regional data residency requirements.

To create a database with the us jurisdiction, run:

For more information, refer to D1 data location.

item.title: KV - Workers KV namespace jurisdictions are now generally available
item.description:
Jurisdictions for Workers KV namespaces are now generally available. When you create a namespace, you can set a jurisdiction to make sure the namespace's data is only durably stored within that region. Jurisdictions can help you comply with data localization regulations such as GDPR or FedRAMP. Supported jurisdictions are eu, us, and fedramp.

A jurisdiction can only be set when a namespace is created, using the Cloudflare dashboard, Wrangler, the cf CLI, or the REST API, and cannot be added or changed afterwards.

Workers can still access a namespace restricted to a jurisdiction from anywhere in the world, and KV data can be cached outside the jurisdiction on Cloudflare's network. The jurisdiction only controls where the namespace's data is durably stored.

To learn more, refer to Data location.

item.title: Workers AI - Introducing Clef: Cloudflare's first open-source decision models, now on Workers AI
item.description:
Meet @cf/cloudflare/clef and @cf/cloudflare/clef-flash, the first models trained by the Cloudflare Workers AI team, available on Workers AI today.

Clef is a decision model, in the same family as Typesafe's Jev ↗︎. Instead of generating text, it reads an input state and a set of typed questions, then returns a probability for every allowed answer. Your agent gets a structured decision it can act on immediately, for example: route the ticket, block the request, or escalate to a human. There is no free-form output to parse and no reasoning tokens to wait for.

Both models are hosted on Workers AI as Clef and Clef-flash. We are also open-sourcing the weights under the Apache 2.0 license on Hugging Face: Clef ↗︎ and Clef-flash ↗︎. Read the launch blog post ↗︎ for the full story, including how we trained them.

We are also launching a reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tuning service to help you tune Clef for your own workloads. Sign up to work with us as a design partner ↗︎.

Built for the hot path

Clef is designed to be fast so decisions come back in milliseconds. Across our 43 benchmark runs, we achieved speeds where Clef is 2.5x faster than Jev at the median, and Clef-flash 13x faster.

Latency Clef Clef-flash Jev
Median 209.3 ms 38.8 ms 524.1 ms
p95 238.6 ms 122.4 ms 536.0 ms

Hosting on Workers AI adds to that speed. Requests run on GPUs across Cloudflare's network, running close to your users, so the network round trip stays short. You can put Clef directly in the request path of your agent, then hand off to an LLM on Workers AI to take action.

Leading the benchmarks

Across 10 decision benchmarks, a Clef model scores highest on 7, ahead of Jev and other open decision models. A few highlights:

Benchmark Clef Clef-flash Jev
BFCL (case exact) 98.47 98.76 95.75
BANKING77 (macro-F1) 94.20 90.93 79.74
CLINC150+OOS (macro-F1) 97.43 66.77 89.27
Home appliances (case exact) 82.95 97.73 52.27

On Typesafe's own workflow evals, Clef beats Jev in 3 of 4 areas: invoice processing, customer service, and security incidents. The full results are on the Hugging Face model card ↗︎.

Drop-in compatible with Jev

Model Size Best for Context window
@cf/cloudflare/clef 27B Highest-precision decisions 64K tokens
@cf/cloudflare/clef-flash 9B Latency-critical, hot-path decisions 64K tokens

Clef follows the System One API, so you can switch an existing Jev integration to Clef by changing the endpoint and model. Ask up to 64 questions per request, in three types:

  • noul: A yes/no question. Returns the probability that the answer is yes.
  • choice: Pick one option from a set you define. Returns the chosen option, a probability per option, and a confidence value.
  • score: Rate against an ordered rubric. Returns a probability-weighted score and a probability per level.

What you can build with decision models

  • Support triage: Decide whether a ticket is urgent and which team owns it, then route it without a human in the loop.
  • Threat intelligence: Classify a website by category. Paired with Browser Run, Clef fetched, rendered, and classified a domain in 2.2 seconds, compared to 4.7 seconds for gpt-oss-120b in the same workflow.
  • Trust and safety: Score user submissions against your own policy rubric and act on the probability.
  • Agent guardrails: Let an agent check "should I take this action?" in tens of milliseconds before calling a tool.
  • Visual classification: Pass up to four images alongside the state. Unlike text-only decision models, Clef has a vision encoder.

Get started

Use Clef through the Workers AI binding (env.AI.run()) or the REST API at /ai/run. You can also use AI Gateway with these endpoints.

For more information, refer to the Clef model page, the Clef-flash model page, and pricing.

item.title: Agents, Workers - The best way to do MCP auth just got better: Workers OAuth Provider goes v1, with a new split API and full support for MCP 2026-07-28
item.description:
@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider ↗︎ is now v1, with a new split API. One Worker acts as the authorization server: it signs users in and issues tokens. Your MCP server acts as the resource server, and can run in another Worker. It validates each token with the authorization server over a Service Binding, without crossing the public Internet.

  • It supports the MCP 2026-07-28 authorization specification ↗︎, including Client ID Metadata Documents ↗︎ and issuer identification ↗︎. It still works with older clients, including those using Dynamic Client Registration ↗︎.
  • insufficientScope() gives you step-up authorization ↗︎ in one line.
  • The authorization server and the resource server can run in different Workers ↗︎ with different WAF and rate limiting rules.
  • One authorization server can issue tokens for many MCP servers ↗︎.
  • A migration skill ↗︎ ships in the npm package so a coding agent can perform the upgrade.

The split API

In the example, env.AUTH_SERVER.validateToken is that Service Binding call. The calendar Worker needs no KV namespace of its own.

OAuthResourceServer publishes the RFC 9728 ↗︎ protected resource metadata that MCP clients use to find your authorization server. It answers requests without a token with a 401 challenge that points to that metadata. It also rejects tokens issued for any other resource.

You can still use OAuthProvider as both the authorization server and the MCP server. For most 0.x deployments, the only required change is to add resourceMetadata: { resource }.

Other updates and helpers

  • Consent page ↗︎ and upstream sign-in ↗︎ helpers implement the MCP confused deputy protections.
  • Sliding refresh token expiry ↗︎ with refreshTokenIdleTTL.
  • Resumable KV cleanup ↗︎ with purgeExpiredData().
  • An internal reason ↗︎ on every error passed to onError.

Upgrade with the migration skill

npm i @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
yarn add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
pnpm add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest
bun add @cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider@latest

Point your coding agent at node_modules/@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider/skills/migrate-to-1.x/SKILL.md, or follow the migration guide ↗︎.

For both Workers in full, refer to the split Workers example ↗︎.

item.title: AI Search - AI Search is generally available
item.description:
AI Search is now generally available. Usage-based billing begins on November 1, 2026, with included monthly ingestion, storage, semantic query, and full-text query usage. Cloudflare will send a reminder email the week before billing begins.

Refer to Limits & pricing for rates and included usage.

Hybrid search is on by default

New AI Search instances use hybrid search by default. Hybrid search combines semantic vector retrieval with full-text matching. You can choose a different index method when you create an instance.

Refer to Hybrid search for details.

Workers AI embeddings and reranking are included

Workers AI embedding and reranking calls made by AI Search are included in AI Search pricing. These calls no longer appear on your Workers AI bill or in your AI Gateway logs. Generation, query rewriting, and external providers continue to use your account and gateway.

Refer to Limits & pricing for details.

Multimodal model and image support

AI Search supports the @cf/qwen/qwen3-vl-embedding-2b and google-ai-studio/gemini-embedding-2 multimodal embedding models. Search and chat requests can include images through the REST API and public endpoint.

Refer to Supported models for the full list of embedding models.

OCR availability and increased file limits

Optical character recognition (OCR) is available on every account for scanned PDFs. Plain-text or code files and PDFs with OCR enabled can be up to 10 MiB. PDFs without OCR and other supported formats remain limited to 4 MiB.

Refer to Data source for file limits and Limits & pricing for OCR pricing.

Source type inference

When you create an AI Search instance, the type field is optional. AI Search infers a website source from an HTTP or HTTPS URL, or an R2 source from an existing bucket name.

Refer to Data source for details.

item.title: Artifacts, Workers - Artifacts is now in open beta
item.description:
Artifacts, Cloudflare's versioned file system that speaks Git, is now in open beta. Artifacts is built for scale, so you can create a repository per project, user, session, or task.

With Artifacts, you can:
